title: Obliquity + Frame bias
description:
Port obliquity (swi_epsiln) and frame bias (swi_bias) from swephlib.c. Both are small, closely related, and have no dependencies beyond the existing math/types modules.

## Obliquity — swi_epsiln (swephlib.c:887)
Pure function: `(tjd, model) → Epsilon { eps, sin_eps, cos_eps }`.
4 models: IAU 1976, IAU 2006, Laskar 1986, Vondrák 2011.
- IAU 1976/2006: polynomial in T (centuries from J2000)
- Laskar 1986: 10th-degree polynomial
- Vondrák 2011: polynomial + periodic terms (same structure as Vondrák precession)
Model selection via AstroModels.

**No caching.** The C code caches oec/oec2000 on the context struct — we don't. Pure function, caller caches if needed.

## Frame bias — swi_bias (swephlib.c:2205)
Pure function: `(x, tjd, model, direction) → x'` — applies GCRS↔J2000 rotation.
3 models: none, IAU 2000, IAU 2006 (default).
Fixed 3×3 matrix multiply. Direction flag controls forward vs inverse.

## Output types
- `Epsilon { tjd: f64, eps: f64, sin_eps: f64, cos_eps: f64 }` in types.rs
- Obliquity function in a new `obliquity.rs` or in `precession.rs` (the placeholder exists)
- Frame bias can go alongside obliquity — it's tiny

## Testing
Golden tests: compute obliquity + frame bias at known epochs (J2000, B1950, far past/future) for each model, compare to C swetest output. Add to the existing golden test harness.

## C source reference
- swephlib.c:887–1370 (swi_epsiln, obliquity coefficients)
- swephlib.c:2205–2260 (swi_bias)

acceptance_criteria.text: frame bias function with all 3 models
golden tests against C for all models at multiple epochs

decisions.decision: All ~11 C obliquity models ported (not just 4)
decisions.rationale: They share the dispatch structure and are mostly just different polynomial coefficients. Porting all now avoids revisiting the module later.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Port only 4 (IAU 1976, Laskar 1986, IAU 2006, Vondrák 2011) — would leave gaps when other precession models are used

decisions.rationale: Precession and nutation also have forward/inverse transforms. One enum, reuse everywhere.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Local to bias module — would require duplication or refactoring when precession/nutation land

decisions.rationale: They are part of the C function's contract. Excluding them would mean golden tests can't cover those code paths, and downstream JPLHOR flag handling would silently differ.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Defer to a separate task — cleaner scope but breaks golden-test completeness

decisions.rationale: 5-line utility used by ~10 obliquity models. Centralizes Horner evaluation, prevents inline duplication.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Inline Horner in each formula — duplicates pattern, risks inconsistent evaluation order

decisions.decision: Epsilon struct has 3 fields (no teps/JD field)
decisions.rationale: No caching means no cache-invalidation field needed. Callers know the JD they passed in.
decisions.rejected_alternative: Include JD field like C struct — adds a field that serves no purpose without caching

execution_record: Ported all 11 C obliquity models (exceeding the 4 originally specified) and all 3 bias models. Key implementation detail: polynomial models must use `* DEGTORAD / 3600.0` (two ops) to match C's runtime evaluation order, while Laskar and Vondrák use `* (DEGTORAD / 3600.0)` (single multiply by precomputed constant) matching C's `eps *= DEGTORAD/3600.0` and `q *= AS2R` patterns. Owen 1990 uses Chebyshev polynomial evaluation with 5 coefficient sets. Golden tests: 205 obliquity cases (bitwise-exact for polynomial models, 1e-15 epsilon for trig-based models) + 17 bias cases (all bitwise-exact).

Codex adversarial review (273d1a1..00f04ee):

Verdict: needs-attention — one high-severity finding.

[high] approx_jplhor() rotates velocities but C only adjusts position. The Rust path uses cartesian_to_polar_with_speed() on the full 6-vector, while C uses position-only swi_cartpol()/swi_polcart(). This means the RA correction affects x[3..6] in Rust but not in C. Golden tests don't exercise JPLHOR_APPROX, so the divergence is untested.

Fix: make JPL Horizons correction position-only (convert/update x[0..3], leave x[3..6] untouched). Add golden fixtures for JPLHOR_APPROX in both FrameTransform directions, with and without SPEED.

messages.text: Fixed approx_jplhor velocity issue (d405b2d). Changed to position-only cartesian_to_polar/polar_to_cartesian (3-vector), matching C's swi_cartpol/swi_polcart. Added 20 JPLHOR_APPROX golden test cases: both directions × with/without SPEED × 5 dates across correction table. All 80 tests pass.
